verdicts.reason: A keeps the original logo, text, CTA order, but the headline has shrunk relative to the canvas, the subline is tiny and far below the headline, and there is dead space above and below. B moves the logo away from the left to float above the CTA, jams the headline and subline against the left edge with almost no margin, and leaves a large empty middle, so the brand reads last and the layout looks lopsided.

A has the same flaws as above (small subline, a loose gap between headline and subline, empty bands at top and bottom) but keeps the banner's left-to-right reading. B stacks everything vertically in a wide banner, shrinks the logo to an illegible speck, and mixes a centered logo and CTA with a left-aligned text block that is off-axis, leaving the right third empty and the CTA crowded near the bottom edge.

The two are nearly identical in structure. B's logo is shrunk and weaker, and its headline sits higher with an even bigger gap above the tiny subline, so the text block reads as two disconnected fragments that don't line up with the CTA. A's logo is larger and its spacing a bit more even, but it has the same small subline and empty bands.
